questions.stem: Find all the cube roots of -8.
questions.solution: The cube root of -8 is -2 because (-2) · (-2) · (-2) = -8.
questions.explanation: Cube roots involve raising a number to the power of 1/3. Since -8 is a perfect cube, it has only one real cube root.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be selecting A (-3), which is incorrect because (-3) · (-3) · (-3) = -27, not -8. Another mistake might be selecting B (2), which is incorrect because 2 is a positive number and the cube root of -8 must be negative.

questions.stem: What are the square roots of 9?
questions.solution: The square roots of 9 are -3 and 3 because (-3) · (-3) = 9 and (3) · (3) = 9.
questions.explanation: Square roots involve raising a number to the power of 1/2. A positive number has two square roots: one positive and one negative.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be selecting C (3), which is only one of the two possible square roots. Another mistake might be selecting D (9), which is not a square root but rather the number itself squared.

questions.stem: Find all the fourth roots of 16.
questions.solution: The fourth roots of 16 are -2 and 2 because (-2) · (-2) · (-2) · (-2) = 16 and (2) · (2) · (2) · (2) = 16.
questions.explanation: Fourth roots involve raising a number to the power of 1/4. A positive number has four fourth roots: two positive and two negative.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be selecting A (-4, -2), which omits the positive fourth root. Another mistake might be selecting D (0), which is not a valid fourth root of 16 because 0 raised to any power other than -1 or a multiple of 2 will never equal 16.

questions.stem: What are the cube roots of 8?
questions.solution: The cube root of 8 is 2 because (2) · (2) · (2) = 8. Since 8 is a perfect cube, it has only one real cube root.
questions.explanation: Cube roots involve raising a number to the power of 1/3. Since 8 is a positive number, its cube root is also positive.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be selecting A (-2, 2), which includes an extraneous negative root. Another mistake might be selecting C (0, 2), which includes an incorrect zero root.

questions.stem: Find all the square roots of -49.
questions.solution: The square root of -49 is -7 because (-7) · (-7) = 49. Since -49 is a negative number, its only real square root is negative.
questions.explanation: Square roots involve raising a number to the power of 1/2. A negative number has one real square root, which is also negative.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be selecting A (7, -7), which includes an extraneous positive root. Another mistake might be selecting C (7) or D (0), both of which are incorrect because they do not yield -49 when squared.

questions.stem: What are the fourth roots of 81?
questions.solution: The fourth roots of 81 are -3 and 3 because (-3) · (-3) · (-3) · (-3) = 81 and (3) · (3) · (3) · (3) = 81.
questions.explanation: Fourth roots involve raising a number to the power of 1/4. A positive number has four fourth roots: two positive and two negative.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be selecting B (3, 9), which includes an extraneous positive root. Another mistake might be selecting C (-3, 9) or D (0), both of which include incorrect roots that do not yield 81 when raised to the fourth power.

questions.stem: Find all the square roots of 64.
questions.solution: The square roots of 64 are -8 and 8 because (-8) · (-8) = 64 and (8) · (8) = 64.
questions.explanation: Square roots involve raising a number to the power of 1/2. A positive number has two square roots: one positive and one negative.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be selecting A (-8, -8), which includes an extraneous duplicate negative root. Another mistake might be selecting B (8, 8) or D (0), both of which include incorrect roots that do not yield 64 when squared.
